title: Bootstrap a working React TypeScript project and passing test
body:
## Goal
A student developer can install, test, and build the empty app.

## Acceptance criteria
### Functional and edge cases
- [ ] React TypeScript shell renders the StudySprint title in an executed DOM component smoke test; production build succeeds.
- [ ] A meaningful smoke or model test actually passes before feature work.
- [ ] Document npm installation, development and test commands.
### Verification and Definition of Done
- [ ] Dependency installation and test/build commands are executed; failures corrected. Local dev-server configuration and command are documented; managed-environment server execution remains unverified.
- [ ] Implemented changes committed; independent QA records acceptance results. Link real issue/commit when available; close only after verification.
### Definition of Done
- [ ] Changes committed with genuine history; actual issue linked when available.
- [ ] Independent QA records acceptance evidence; failures fixed before closure.

## Out of scope
No assignment features.

## Constraints
None; product and technical documents precede this task.
Implementation follows `_docs/architecture.md`; no paid services, accounts or additional feature scope. Tests follow `_docs/testing-guidelines.md`. Draft numbers identify dependency order, not real GitHub issue numbers.

title: Implement validated assignment CRUD and safe persistence
body:
## Goal
As a student I can save and maintain coursework without losing valid records.

## Acceptance criteria
### Functional behavior
- [ ] Task schema has unique string id, title, subject, dueDate, priority, notes, completed and createdAt.
- [ ] Create generates a unique stable ID and genuine createdAt timestamp.
- [ ] Trim title and subject before validation and saving.
- [ ] Title accepts 1–120 characters after trimming; rejects blank or 121+.
- [ ] Subject accepts 1–80 characters after trimming; rejects blank or 81+.
- [ ] Notes are optional and accept at most 2000 characters.
- [ ] Priority is exactly low, medium or high; default medium is visible.
- [ ] Due date is an actual local calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD format.
- [ ] Past due dates are accepted as valid assignment dates; impossible dates are rejected.
- [ ] Edit updates the existing ID rather than adding a duplicate.
- [ ] Editing does not unexpectedly change completion or createdAt.
- [ ] Complete marks a task completed; reopen restores it to active.
- [ ] Delete asks confirmation; cancellation leaves all tasks unchanged.
- [ ] Confirmed deletion removes only the selected task.

### Failure and persistence
- [ ] Validation errors are visible near fields and prevent mutation.
- [ ] Saved tasks survive browser refresh.
- [ ] Missing storage initializes an empty state.
- [ ] Malformed stored JSON/schema is handled without application crash.
- [ ] Corrupt storage is reported visibly and not silently presented as valid data.
- [ ] Storage write/quota failure is visible; never falsely claim successful persistence.
- [ ] A failed storage write preserves prior saved records.
- [ ] Task text is rendered safely without raw HTML.

### Verification
- [ ] Automated tests exercise trim/blank/maximum lengths and date validity.
- [ ] Automated tests cover edit identity, completion/reopen and storage validation.
- [ ] Testing Library component integration tests exercise create/edit/delete/complete and persisted reload behavior.

### Definition of Done
- [ ] Changes committed with genuine history; actual issue linked when available.
- [ ] Independent QA records acceptance evidence; failures fixed before closure.

## Out of scope
Cloud accounts and sync. Overdue classification and display are implemented and verified in follow-up draft 03 (`_docs/issues/03.md`); this CRUD issue only validates and stores past dates.

## Constraints
Depends on issue draft 01; stable model and centralized storage.
Implementation follows `_docs/architecture.md`; no paid services, accounts or additional feature scope. Tests follow `_docs/testing-guidelines.md`. Draft numbers identify dependency order, not real GitHub issue numbers.

title: Build responsive dashboard, search, filters and sorting
body:
## Goal
As a student I can identify urgent coursework and find the right task.

## Acceptance criteria
### Dashboard
- [ ] Total count includes all tasks.
- [ ] Completed count includes only completed tasks.
- [ ] Overdue count includes only active tasks with date before local today.
- [ ] Due-today count includes active tasks due on the local current date.
- [ ] Counts remain unchanged when list search/filter changes.
- [ ] Completed past-date tasks are excluded from urgency counts.

### Finding tasks
- [ ] Search matches title, subject and notes case-insensitively.
- [ ] Empty search restores all otherwise matching tasks.
- [ ] Status filter supports all, active and completed.
- [ ] Priority filter supports all, low, medium and high.
- [ ] Search and both filters combine rather than overwrite each other.
- [ ] Due-date sort orders earlier dates first.
- [ ] Priority sort orders high before medium before low.
- [ ] Equal sort keys produce deterministic ordering.
- [ ] Sorting preserves the underlying records and IDs.
- [ ] Filtered no-results state explains how to adjust filters.

### Accessibility and layout
- [ ] Empty task state provides a clear create action.
- [ ] Every form/filter input has a persistent associated label.
- [ ] Buttons use native keyboard activation and visible focus.
- [ ] Urgency and priority have text labels in addition to color.
- [ ] Responsive CSS defines stacked phone layout, min-width constraints and wrapping; actual browser overflow verification remains unverified.
- [ ] Desktop CSS defines readable assignment panels; timer-panel integration is delivered in follow-up draft 04.
- [ ] CSS wraps long titles/notes and preserves native controls in DOM; actual visual clipping verification remains unverified.

### Verification
- [ ] Unit tests cover combined search/filter/sort and date counts.
- [ ] Inspect responsive CSS/source and DOM structure; record actual browser viewport inspection as unavailable unless executed.
- [ ] DOM integration verifies associated labels and keyboard-operable native controls; visual focus/viewport inspection remains an explicit external limitation.

### Definition of Done
- [ ] Changes committed with genuine history; actual issue linked when available.
- [ ] Independent QA records acceptance evidence; failures fixed before closure.

## Out of scope
Charts and notifications. Timer-panel integration belongs to follow-up draft 04 (`_docs/issues/04.md`). Actual browser overflow, clipping and visual readability checks are unverified external inspection requirements; source/DOM verification does not certify their outcome.

## Constraints
Depends on 02; browser local calendar dates.
Implementation follows `_docs/architecture.md`; no paid services, accounts or additional feature scope. Tests follow `_docs/testing-guidelines.md`. Draft numbers identify dependency order, not real GitHub issue numbers.

title: Implement linked focus timer and session history
body:
## Goal
As a student I can focus on one task and track finished study sessions.

## Acceptance criteria
### Timer lifecycle
- [ ] Duration accepts integers from 1 through 120 minutes inclusive.
- [ ] Reject zero, negative, fractional, nonnumeric and 121+ minute values.
- [ ] Default duration is visibly 25 minutes.
- [ ] Timer can be linked to one existing task or no task.
- [ ] Start begins countdown from configured duration.
- [ ] Pause stops decrementing while retaining remaining time.
- [ ] Resume continues from remaining time.
- [ ] Reset stops timer and restores selected configured duration.
- [ ] Only one active countdown loop exists after repeated start/resume.
- [ ] Component cleanup clears timers.
- [ ] Zero crossing stops countdown without negative displayed time.
- [ ] One completed countdown appends exactly one completed session.
- [ ] Session has unique ID, optional task ID, durationMinutes and completedAt.
- [ ] Pause/reset does not record a completed session.

### Persistence and edge cases
- [ ] Settings and completed session history persist after reload.
- [ ] Refresh restores remaining timer snapshot paused.
- [ ] Refresh does not count elapsed wall time or auto-complete a session.
- [ ] Deleting linked task detaches or safely resolves the timer link.
- [ ] History remains readable when its task was deleted.
- [ ] Completion is announced meaningfully without announcing every tick.
- [ ] Storage failure remains visible and does not crash countdown.

### Verification
- [ ] Test duration boundaries and exactly-once completion.
- [ ] Check pause/resume/reset and task deletion.
- [ ] Check reload restores paused remaining time and history.
- [ ] Use executed fake-timer component integration tests for timer lifecycle; no fabricated browser observations.

### Definition of Done
- [ ] Changes committed with genuine history; actual issue linked when available.
- [ ] Independent QA records acceptance evidence; failures fixed before closure.

## Out of scope
Background notifications and cross-device sync.

## Constraints
Depends on 02 and 03; clear interval cleanup and no duplicate sessions.
Implementation follows `_docs/architecture.md`; no paid services, accounts or additional feature scope. Tests follow `_docs/testing-guidelines.md`. Draft numbers identify dependency order, not real GitHub issue numbers.

title: Add validated backup import/export and optional demo data
body:
## Goal
As a student I can transfer my data and try the application safely.

## Acceptance criteria
### Export
- [ ] Export is a user-triggered JSON file download.
- [ ] Backup schemaVersion is exactly 1.
- [ ] Backup contains tasks, sessions and settings consistent with current app state.
- [ ] Optional timer snapshot is either validated or omitted consistently.
- [ ] Export preserves task IDs, completion and session timestamps.

### Atomic import
- [ ] Read selected JSON and reject parsing failures visibly.
- [ ] Reject unsupported schemaVersion before replacing data.
- [ ] Reject missing required collections/settings or wrong types.
- [ ] Validate every task, including title/subject lengths, date, priority and boolean completion.
- [ ] Reject duplicate task IDs and duplicate session IDs.
- [ ] Validate session duration range and completion timestamp.
- [ ] Validate configured focus duration as integer 1–120.
- [ ] Validate optional timer remaining seconds and task references according to documented policy.
- [ ] Malformed record in otherwise valid backup rejects entire import.
- [ ] Show replacement confirmation only after complete validation.
- [ ] Cancel replacement leaves tasks, sessions, settings and timer unchanged.
- [ ] Confirmed valid replacement applies complete backup atomically.
- [ ] Invalid import leaves original state and saved data unchanged.
- [ ] Storage error does not falsely report a successful saved replacement.
- [ ] Import errors clearly explain failure and allow retry.

### Demo and verification
- [ ] Demo seeding is an explicit action.
- [ ] Demo never overwrites a nonempty task collection.
- [ ] Demo produces realistic valid tasks useful for demonstrating urgency.
- [ ] Automated tests exercise malformed/version/type/date/ID/range cases.
- [ ] Automated tests exercise valid export/import roundtrip.
- [ ] Component integration tests exercise export payload and replacement-confirmation cancellation.

### Definition of Done
- [ ] Changes committed with genuine history; actual issue linked when available.
- [ ] Independent QA records acceptance evidence; failures fixed before closure.

## Out of scope
Merge conflict resolution or cloud backup.

## Constraints
Depends on 02 and 04; atomic replacement, clear errors.
Implementation follows `_docs/architecture.md`; no paid services, accounts or additional feature scope. Tests follow `_docs/testing-guidelines.md`. Draft numbers identify dependency order, not real GitHub issue numbers.

title: Verify MVP, accessibility and final submission documentation
body:
## Goal
As a reviewer I can reproduce and assess the locally completed MVP; public submission is a separate follow-up.

## Acceptance criteria
### Documentation
- [ ] README identifies app purpose and MVP features.
- [ ] README gives exact install/dev/test/build commands.
- [ ] README explains local-only storage, backups and refresh-paused timer.
- [ ] README has a reproducible demonstration sequence.
- [ ] AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, plan/process/task template/team roles exist and contain project-specific content.
- [ ] Technology, architecture, design and testing docs match implemented behavior.
- [ ] chat-brainstorm.md contains genuine available messages and separates assistant defaults.
- [ ] No fabricated interview answers, commits or QA results appear.
- [ ] Video/example access gaps are documented honestly.

### Actual validation
- [ ] Execute automated suite and record command, totals and outcome.
- [ ] Execute production build and fix errors.
- [ ] Execute typecheck if configured and record actual result.
- [ ] Execute component integration checks for task creation/edit/delete/complete and persisted state restoration.
- [ ] Execute DOM integration and pure logic checks for dashboard/filter/sort behavior.
- [ ] Execute fake-timer component integration checks for pause/resume/reset and completed history.
- [ ] Execute component integration checks for valid/invalid import, cancellation and demo non-overwrite.
- [ ] Inspect responsive CSS and associated labels/native controls in DOM; record unavailable real-browser visual/keyboard checks as limitations.
- [ ] Document all unexecuted real-browser checks separately; local QA closure does not claim visual verification.
- [ ] Fix reproducible defects and rerun affected checks.

### Local handoff readiness
- [ ] GitHub publication is tracked in draft 07 and remains blocked until actual remote verification.
- [ ] Final compliance distinguishes completed, provisional and inaccessible requirements.

### Definition of Done
- [ ] Changes committed with genuine history; actual issue linked when available.
- [ ] Independent QA records acceptance evidence; failures fixed before closure.

## Out of scope
Claiming unavailable video or fake GitHub activity.

## Constraints
Depends on 01–05; final timestamps must be compared privately with the current supplied cutoff.
Implementation follows `_docs/architecture.md`; no paid services, accounts or additional feature scope. Tests follow `_docs/testing-guidelines.md`. Draft numbers identify dependency order, not real GitHub issue numbers.

title: Publish public GitHub repository and verify issue history
body:
## Goal
Publish the verified local StudySprint MVP to a real public GitHub repository and establish traceable issue history. This is a blocked follow-up until GitHub authentication is available; local readiness does not imply publication.

## Acceptance criteria
### Remote publication
- [ ] Authenticated GitHub account and target repository are identified without exposing credentials.
- [ ] Repository is actually created and confirmed public by API/CLI readback.
- [ ] Sanitized deliverables and genuine new publication commits are pushed; remote branch head matches the public staging snapshot.
- [ ] Actual issues are created using the groomed draft bodies, including this publication follow-up.
- [ ] Real issue numbers replace dependency placeholders; draft numbers are not presented as real issue IDs.
- [ ] Each local implementation issue receives an honest comment linking the verified public snapshot and executed local QA evidence; private development commit IDs are not represented as public commits.
- [ ] Issue closure occurs only after acceptance evidence exists and real close action succeeds.
- [ ] Publication issue itself is closed only after all remote checks succeed.
### Deadline and final evidence
- [ ] Read genuine createdAt/closedAt and compare privately against the current privately supplied cutoff; publish no cutoff or comparison result.
- [ ] Report any late issue honestly; do not backdate commits or issues.
- [ ] Record working repository and real issue URLs and read-back states.
- [ ] Final compliance retains inaccessible video, incomplete interview, and unavailable real-browser inspection as unresolved limitations.
- [ ] If authentication or deadline prevents success, leave this follow-up blocked and provide exact user-run commands rather than claim completion.

## Out of scope
Fabricating GitHub events, altering timestamps, or claiming unavailable source/video/browser verification.

## Constraints
Depends on local drafts 01–06. Use GitHub CLI/API only with authorized account access. Publish only genuine commits and documented evidence. Real issue creation order, mapping, closure and readback must be auditable. The user reported an extension; exact current timing is privately supplied during publication, never echoed or published. Original development history is retained privately; new public commits describe publication stages, not reconstructed development chronology. Do not close this issue based solely on local files or a prepared script.
